title: Ingham's theorem: zero-free half-planes of the Riemann zeta function and the error term in the prime number theorem
abstract: For 1/2 ≤ θ < 1, the Riemann zeta function has no zeros with real part greater than θ if and only if Chebyshev's ψ(x) = x + O(x^{θ+δ}) for every δ > 0. Consequences: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2+δ}) for all δ > 0, and the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 (proved by OpenAI in 2026, used here as an explicitly stated hypothesis) yields ψ(x) = x + O(x^{7/8+δ}). Both directions are proved: the easy direction by partial summation and holomorphy of a Mellin transform; the hard direction by a smoothed Chebyshev function, a contour shift to a vertical line inside the zero-free half-plane, and a bound ζ'/ζ(σ+it) ≪ log|t| obtained from the Borel–Carathéodory theorem.
